pos.personaBrief: Napoli led Serie A in passes (642 per game) and used possession to disorganise opponents (Juego de Posicion), with the high line and counter-press keeping the ball. Possession was the control tool, not a counter-attacking trap.

pro.personaBrief: Short build-up from goalkeeper with Jorginho dropping between centre-backs, but the mantra was always seek the forward pass, ground ball and fast transitions, with central progressions.

est.personaBrief: Spielverlagerung describes staggered positioning and half-space circulation with rehearsed rotations (Hamsik, Ghoulam, Insigne), tight combinations on the left and wingers drifting inside.

lar.personaBrief: Width came from full-backs while Insigne, Callejon and Mertens moved inside; Napoli ranked 19th in positive cross percentage, preferring central progression to open wide areas.

blo.personaBrief: Highest defensive line in Serie A (38.2m recoveries), immediate counter-press and aggressive forwards pressing centre-backs back to Buffon.

mar.personaBrief: Ball-oriented positional defending with players adjusting to ball and teammates and Sarri zonal corners; no evidence of dedicated man-markers, though marking is only inferred.

pla.personaBrief: Sarri imposed a fixed game model on arrival and stuck to it against all opponents, adjusting only after the 4-3-1-2 failed; he kept the same plan and the same XI.

res.personaBrief: Sarri refuses the offensivist or defensivist labels but the team played proactive, attractive football and sought to win away, finishing with 91 points as runner-up.

sis.personaBrief: A collective model that lifted players like Albiol and turned Mertens into a striker; stars like Higuain and Insigne had defined roles, and Sarri benched Insigne when he complained.

jog.personaBrief: Sarri admitted having the lightest team in the league; technique and passing (Jorginho, Hamsik, Insigne) over strength.

bas.personaBrief: Small, stable squad of established players (Albiol, Hamsik, Callejon), little rotation and minimal academy focus; the goal was consistency to win.

lid.personaBrief: Sarri held authority: he removed Insigne and told him to apologise to teammates, and demanded the same rules from everyone, while players like Mertens praised him.
